The hidden cost of loose components

Loose parts are a kitting and quality problem wearing a packaging disguise

Tray, tube and bulk components cannot feed a pick-and-place line directly. Manual repacking is slow, inconsistent and invisible to quality systems.

Manual repacking is a bench job

Operators place components into carrier tape by hand — a slow, error-prone task that scales only with headcount.

Empty pockets ship silently

A missed pocket in a reel means a skipped placement and a failed board at your mounter.

Seal quality varies by hand

Hand-sealed cover tape peels or shifts; components move in transit and misplace on the line.

Kitting bottlenecks the line

The mounter waits on repacked reels — and the repack bench becomes the schedule.

ESD and handling risk

Loose handling of sensitive components risks ESD damage and bent leads before they ever reach the line.

No traceability

Manual repacking leaves no record of which lot went into which reel.

Installation guide

From bench to production in five steps

Installation and operator training are included free with every taping machine.

01 · Bench & layout

Place the machine on a stable workbench with room for the supply reels (carrier tape, cover tape) and the take-up spool. Mains power nearby.

02 · Utilities

Connect AC220 V (400 W) and compressed air at 0.4–0.6 MPa. The machine is benchtop weight (35 kg) and needs no special foundation.

03 · Setup & calibration

Load empty carrier tape, set track width for your tape (8–72 mm or 8–200 mm), set seal temperature per cover-tape side and verify the EPD sensor.

04 · Trial run

Pack sample components, check pocket seating and seal quality (heat or pressure seal), and adjust speed (up to 400 m/h) for your component mix.

05 · Training & ramp

Free installation and operator training included; 24/7 worldwide support and 1-day spare-part lead time.

Buyer's FAQ

Questions buyers ask before choosing a taping machine

What does a semi-auto taping machine actually do?

It repacks components from trays, tubes or bulk into embossed carrier tape and seals them with cover tape (heat or pressure seal), producing ready-to-feed reels for your pick-and-place machine. The SJL80A does this automatically up to 400 meters per hour under touch-screen control.

Which component types can be taped?

Radial parts, semiconductors, passives and even mechanical parts that fit embossed carrier tape pockets. The automatic family extends this: S-120FC for SMD forming and taping, S-250ART for axial components, S-300BSTD for radial components, S-300RT for spring contacts, S-350 for flat terminals and S-60TP for gas-discharge tubes.

What tape widths does the SJL80A handle?

8 to 72 mm and 8 to 200 mm carrier tapes, with a screw-driven adjustable track for quick changeover between widths.

How does empty-pocket detection work?

The EPD function detects a pocket with no component and raises an alarm (starvation detection), while a low-cover-tape sensor warns before the cover tape runs out — so empty pockets and incomplete reels do not reach your mounter.

What utilities does it need?

AC220 V mains (400 W) and compressed air at 0.4–0.6 MPa. The machine is a 35 kg benchtop unit — no special foundation.

How do I get a quote and packaging recommendation?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your component samples or drawings, package format (tray/tube/bulk) and monthly volume. Configuration, quotation and a packaging-process recommendation are provided within 24 hours.
